content.text: The termination provision is contained entirely in paragraph 4 (p0016); no Exhibit termination terms are attached, and the commercial arrangement is a revenue share (AP receives payments from Kubient), so there are no prepaid fees or early-termination fees at stake.

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) The Initial Term is only one (1) year, so the absence of a mid-term convenience right does not trigger the "term longer than 12 months" / multi-year walk-away test; thereafter AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice, within the fallback's 60–90 day band. (2) There is no early-termination fee or penalty on AP — Kubient is only entitled to fees generated during the 90-day notice period, i.e. revenue actually earned while it is still performing, not a termination charge; and because fees are a revenue share paid by Kubient to AP (para. 5), there are no prepaid fees requiring a pro-rata refund. (3) Kubient's convenience right is symmetrical and requires the full ninety (90) days' notice, so it is not in walk-away territory (which is vendor notice of fewer than 90 days). Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted but not flagged: AP has no 30-day convenience right during the Initial Term, and Kubient's post-Initial-Term convenience right is not confined to the end of a renewal term, so Kubient could exit mid-renewal-year on 90 days' notice. If this agreement is later extended to a multi-year committed term or an Exhibit adds AP-side fees, we should revisit and add a 30-day AP convenience right with a pro-rata refund and strip Kubient's mid-term exit.
